# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 50 (Bi-Vb Pc50)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc50
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 50
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Tiracchānavijjāvācana Sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 50) establishes that a nun who teaches pointless knowledge or worldly arts (*tiracchānavijjā*) incurs an offense that requires confession (*pācittiya*). The rule forms a direct pair with the immediately preceding regulation (Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 49, on learning worldly subjects): its phrasing, word analysis, casuistry, and exemption clauses are identical in structure to Pācittiya 49, differing only in the governing verb *vāceyya* ("teaches") where the former has *pariyāpuneyya* ("learns") [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 In these comparative traditions, the parallel to this rule likewise follows directly upon the parallel prohibiting the learning of worldly arts [Hüsken 1997].
